answer: Residual reputation decay curve. Each identity’s reputation decays toward a floor at a fixed rate unless refreshed by verified activity; the curve’s slope steepens with the number of identities sharing one funding source, so marginal identities sit on a lower terrace of usable trust. An attacker must keep every fake identity active enough to stay above the orchard of viable agents, paying continuous refresh costs that rise superlinearly with fleet size. Any single ember of inactivity drops that identity below threshold. Cost is recurring, not one-time.
